HaramBlur · OfflineBlur · trial report · 17 September 2026

Blurring adult women in Dawah street videos, offline

What was built, what it did on three clips, what broke, and what changed because of it. All runs on a RunPod RTX PRO 6000 (96 GB). Nothing here is a benchmark; it is two pieces of real footage looked at frame by frame.

1. The job and its rules

Input: a recorded Dawah video (street interview, Speakers Corner, 2 minutes to hours). Output: the same video with every adult woman pixelated (audio kept), a white-on-black matte, and per-frame masks with identity ids so an editor can composite their own effect. It runs offline on a GPU; accuracy is the only thing that matters.

priority 1No false blurNever a poster, statue, sign or background object; never a man.
priority 2No escapeA woman is blurred in every frame she is visible: partial, small, side-on, from behind, through occlusions.
priority 3Pixel-accurate, stable masksFollow the person, never flicker, never bleed onto the person next to her.
neverChildren and menChildren 12 or younger are never blurred. Men are never blurred.

2. The pipeline (v1.4, current)

The design principle after five iterations: find people with one model, decide who they are from many frames, and decide the class before linking, so a bad link can never turn a woman into a man. Every stage writes plain files, so later stages re-run in seconds without touching the GPU-heavy detection.

stage 1Detect + segment + trackYOLO11x-seg at 1280 px on every frame, BoT-SORT with re-identification. Logs every tracked person with a full-resolution pixel mask.
stage 2SegmentsCut tracks where the tracker probably switched person (motion-predicted gap check). Per segment: 8 crops spread over its life, OSNet body embedding, ArcFace face embedding on the upscaled crop, sliver and duplicate measures.
stage 3Judge every cropQwen2.5-VL-7B answers per crop: real person / poster / not a person; man or woman; child or adult. Face-visible crops weigh ×3, slivers weigh 0.
stage 4IdentitiesDecide each segment's class, then link segments: mask duplicates → host; face ≥ 0.45; body ≥ 0.85 + motion + same class; geometric handoff. Decide each identity from all its crops.
stage 5RenderPer-identity mask, dilated 2 % of height, unioned over ±1 frame, feathered, pixelated. Matte + RLE mask export for every human identity.
stage 6Review pageOne card per identity, uncertain ones first, with its crops and votes.

Why this and not the heavy design

The earlier Innovation-lab design (three detectors, SAM 2 masklets, three judges, offline graph tracking) turned a 12-second street interview into 24 mostly-uncertain identities. Fragments break the per-person vote and cause flicker, so identity stability had to be solved first, with as few moving parts as possible. SAM 2 mask refinement, a second detector and a second judge remain the v2 candidates, added only where stage 1 proves too weak.

4. Clip 2 — Ali Dawah at Speakers Corner (day, 360p, first 240 s)

Daytime crowd, about 40 distinct people over four minutes. Ali Dawah in a grey jacket interviewing a woman in a white top; a woman in black with glasses at the right edge for most of the clip; boys in the background. Downloaded from a Dailymotion mirror because YouTube refuses the pod's address; only 640×360 was available, which makes most background people 30 to 65 px tall.

What clip 2 changed in the code

  • Box containment is not evidence of a duplicate. The interviewee stands near the camera, so background people's boxes fall inside hers; the box rule attached 23 fragments (arms, shoulders, far pedestrians) to her and blurred them. Only mask-overlap duplicates attach now.
  • Tiny faces bridge people. A 0.2 s, 40 px fragment with one detected face linked a man to the woman in black at 0.52 similarity. Face links now need ≥ 2 face crops on both sides; crossing a gender lean needs ≥ 0.60 and ≥ 3 faces each. Uncertain leans block links the same way decided classes do.
  • Uncertain blur needs evidence. A 1:1 vote on an arm-shaped mask was blurred for 10.9 s. Gender-uncertain identities are blurred only with a winning share ≥ 0.60, vote weight ≥ 2 and ≥ 0.5 s on screen; the rest go to review. Age-only doubt never unblurs (an adult read as a child is the consequential error).
  • The vote-height floor scales with the frame. 80 px is a third of the height at 360p and silenced every background person; it is now max(48 px, 10 % of frame height).

Run D — the same clip with the frame-relative vote floor

Lowering the floor to 48 px at 360p let 43 more background people be judged (Man 78 → 130, unjudged 108 → 65) with no new false woman blur; 9 women blurred, none uncertain, all nine verified on the sheet. One new defect: a 7-second track starts on a boy in a red shirt for a few frames before the tracker hops onto the woman in black, and the pooled vote blurs the boy briefly. That became the single-frame hop split in v1.4 (below).

What clip 3 changed in the code (v1.4)

  • A face-weighted answer cannot outvote plain ones. The winning share is the mean of the weighted share and the count share; a face crop weighs ×2, not ×3.
  • Handoffs only for segments with no gender lean of their own, and only on a real box overlap (IoU ≥ 0.3), never containment.
  • Single-frame hops split a track. A jump of more than the person's own height between consecutive frames is the tracker hopping onto someone else (the boy → woman case on clip 2).

6. Where it stands

Works: the main subjects of a Dawah video (interviewer, interviewee) are one stable identity each, judged from dozens of frames, with masks that separate the woman from the man next to her. Children and men in frame are left alone. Every decision is inspectable on the review page.
Not solved: a woman partly hidden behind the foreground person is a separate fragment the judge reads as "man" (1.4 s escape on clip 1); a woman the judge splits 4:4 on is left unblurred and flagged (3.8 s on clip 3). Background people smaller than ~10 % of the frame height get no verdict. Fragments are harmless for the blur but noisy for review.

Next

  • HD sources only from here (the mirrors that the pod can reach top out at 720p; true 1080p needs owner-supplied files). On the 720p clip the pipeline judged 178 of 191 identities; on the 360p clip only 92 of 200.
  • A second judge for the ties: MiVOLO V2 (face + body, no language) as an independent vote where Qwen2.5-VL splits evenly.
  • An occlusion rule: a fragment that emerges from behind a large foreground box within a couple of seconds of an identity disappearing there inherits that identity.
  • A second, non-language judge (MiVOLO V2, face + body) for back views, where Qwen2.5-VL is the weakest link.
  • SAM 2 mask refinement only if edge quality becomes the complaint; on these clips the segmentation head's masks were clean.

Files: OfflineBlur/reports/ holds the per-clip markdown reports and the running findings log; each run's review page, contact sheets and videos are under OfflineBlur/out/ and on the pod under /root/offlineblur/out/.
